content.text: This is callback-style DB access with a matching `UserRepository`, which is exactly what the migrate-module skill handles.

Base directory for this skill: <run-dir>/.claude/skills/migrate-module

# Repository pattern migration

The mapping table from callback call to repository method:

| Callback call in a service | Repository method |
|---|---|
| `query('users', u => u.deleted_at === null, cb)` | `UserRepository.findActive()` |
| `query('users', u => u.id === id, cb)` | `UserRepository.findById(id)` |
| `update('users', id, { deleted_at }, cb)` | `UserRepository.softDelete(id, when)` |
| `query('orders', o => o.user_id === id ..., cb)` | `OrderRepository.findByUser(id)` |
| `query('orders', o => o.status === 'paid' ..., cb)` | `OrderRepository.findPaid()` |

Steps:

1. Read the target service file and its test file.
2. Replace every direct `query`/`update` import and call with the matching repository method.
3. Convert the exported functions to return promises. Update the test file to await them.
4. Run only that module's tests: `node --test tests/<module>.test.js`.
5. Stop after three failed attempts and report what blocked you.

`payments` has no repository yet. If the target is `payment-service.js`, create
`src/repositories/payment-repository.js` following the shape of the other two.

content.text:
I couldn't make the changes because write permission was denied on all three files, so nothing has been modified. I didn't run the tests either, since there was nothing to test yet.

`user-service.js` uses the old callback style with direct `query`/`update` calls. The fix is to switch it to the existing `UserRepository`, which has a matching method for each call. Here's what I was going to do:

1. **`src/services/user-service.js`**: drop the direct database imports and call `UserRepository` instead. `findActive()` replaces the active-users query, `findById(id)` replaces the user lookup, and `softDelete(id, when)` replaces the soft delete. All three functions would then return promises instead of taking a callback.
2. **`tests/user-service.test.js`**: change the two tests to `await` the results instead of using callbacks.
3. **`src/api/routes.js`**: this file also needs a change. The `/users` and `/users/:id` routes still pass a callback to `listActiveUsers` and `findUser`. Once those return promises, the callback would never be called and both endpoints would stop responding, even though the unit tests would still pass. I'd add a small helper, `toCallback(promise, cb)`, so those two routes keep working with the router.

After the edits I'd run `node --test tests/user-service.test.js` and `node scripts/check-routes.js` to confirm the module and both routes work.

If you allow writes to those three files, I'll apply this and run both checks. If you'd rather leave `routes.js` alone for now, I can do the service and test changes only, but those two endpoints will break until the routes are updated.
